analysis: Examined base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 1-818 together with the patch excerpt. This is a documentation-only change. The changes visible in the patch cover three places. Head lines 14-16: waiting_inventory now says a verified update prefetch can add a new ID to the Autopilot set, in addition to `darkbloom autopilot models`. Head line 781: autopilot status now documents 'Also downloaded' (verified downloaded catalog builds the running provider adds to the Autopilot set) and 'Downloads' (Autopilot download enablement, limits, usage and free disk). Head lines 786-787 and 821-825: changed, but the bounded patch excerpt does not show them. No source code is in this batch. The doc change implies new runtime behavior. Autopilot may now download models itself. The running provider may extend the Autopilot set beyond the recorded consent inventory to include verified downloaded builds. Base lines 816-818 describe the recorded inventory as an exact-build allowlist, so consent and allowlist semantics may be widening. This is relevant to model-weight integrity: the docs state the builds are 'verified', which ties to T-012/T-027/A-004. It is also relevant to disk exhaustion (T-016) and operator consent. None of the supplied evidence establishes a concrete regression. Integration should confirm three things. First, that the provider-swift Autopilot source (e.g. StartCommand+Autopilot.swift, model-autopilot code) verifies prefetched or added builds against the manifest/registry hash before adding them to the set. Second, that download limits and free-disk guards are enforced. Third, that shadow mode still does not alter residency. The unseen head ranges 786-787 and 821-825 should also be reviewed. No change touches the cache (T-041), logout (A-008/T-053) or attestation sections.
